chapter_title: Unit 2: Wit and Humour (Animals, Birds, and Dr. Dolittle & A Funny Man)

questions.question_text: Where does Dr. John Dolittle reside in Hugh Lofting's story?
Who teaches Dr. Dolittle the language of animals?
In bird language, what does 'Ka-ka oi-ee, fee-fee' mean?
options: Option A: Where is my nest?
Option B: Is the porridge hot yet?
Option C: Look at the cat
Option D: It is going to rain
questions.correct_answer: Option B: Is the porridge hot yet?

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a closed compound word?
In 'A Funny Man', where does the funny man wear his hats?
Why did the Cat's-food-Man suggest that Dr. Dolittle become an animal doctor?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Because Dr. Dolittle understood animals deeply, whereas human patients complained ungratefully despite good care, and local veterinarians lacked true empathy for animals.

questions.question_text: How do animals communicate non-verbally according to Polynesia?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Animals communicate using physical signetics like twitching nostrils, flattening ears, wagging tails, moving eyelids, and flaring nostrils.

questions.question_text: Categorize the compound words: flowerpots, harvest mice, check-in.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Closed Compound: flowerpots
2. Open Compound: harvest mice
3. Hyphenated Compound: check-in

questions.question_text:
Read the extract and answer:
'“If I say, 'Polly wants a cracker', you understand me. But hear this: Ka-ka oi-ee, fee-fee?” “Good Gracious!” cried the Doctor. “What does that mean?”'
(a) Who is speaking to the Doctor?
(b) What does 'Ka-ka oi-ee, fee-fee' mean?
(c) What action did the speaker take after saying this?
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) Polynesia the parrot.
(b) It means 'Is the porridge hot yet?' in bird language.
(c) She dusted cracker crumbs off her wing and explained silent animal signetics.

questions.question_text: Analyze how Dr. Dolittle's patient-centered approach revolutionized his veterinary practice.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Dr. Dolittle listened directly to his animal patients in their native tongues rather than relying on generic medicines. By taking notes on bird vocabulary in his butcher's book, he diagnosed pugs, cows, and horses accurately, building a renowned practice based on empathy.

questions.question_text: What book did Dr. Dolittle fetch to record animal vocabulary?
What illness did the Cat's-food-Man suffer from when visiting Dr. Dolittle?
How does the funny man address the speaker in Natalie Joan's poem?
Which of the following is an open compound word?
What food is the funny man eating as he walks?
Why had Polynesia never spoken bird language to Dr. Dolittle before?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Because Polynesia knew Dr. Dolittle would not have understood bird language until he showed genuine interest in learning animal linguistics.

questions.question_text: Describe the physical actions of the funny man in Natalie Joan's poem.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: The funny man wears two hats on his feet, walks and hops home upside down on his head, eats a currant bun while staggering, and bows politely to passersby.

questions.question_text: How does the present perfect tense function in grammar? Give an example.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: The present perfect tense connects a past action with the present moment (Structure: has/have + past participle). Example: 'Dr. Dolittle has learned bird language.'

questions.question_text: Examine how Natalie Joan creates humor through physical inversion and formal dialogue in 'A Funny Man'.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Humor is created by juxtaposing absurd physical inversion (wearing hats on feet, hopping on head) with formal courtly etiquette ('Your Highness'). The unexpected contrast between aristocratic manners and silly physical posture produces visual and linguistic wit.

questions.question_text: Case Study: A pet owner notices their cat scratching furniture and assumes it is being naughty. How would Dr. Dolittle analyze this behavior?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Dr. Dolittle would decode the cat's non-verbal communication, recognizing that scratching is a natural signetic behavior to mark territory and stretch muscles rather than disobedience. He would advise providing dedicated scratching posts rather than scolding the animal.

questions.question_text: Which type of compound word is 'Cat's-food-Man'?
What action does a dog perform with its nose to ask a question silently?
What is the past participle form of the verb 'write' used in present perfect tense?
Who brought pugs to Dr. Dolittle's surgery?
How does the funny man travel home at the end of the poem?
options: Option B: Hopping on his head
questions.correct_answer: Option B: Hopping on his head

questions.question_text: Explain the rules for constructing Closed, Open, and Hyphenated compound words.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Closed compounds merge two words without spaces (windowsill). Open compounds keep a space between words (bird language). Hyphenated compounds join words with hyphens (well-bred).

questions.question_text: What types of animals were brought to Dr. Dolittle by local farmers?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Farmers brought working animals like cows with eye troubles, sheep, and plough horses needing proper care and spectacles.

questions.question_text: Identify two examples of Alliteration in 'A Funny Man'.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. 'funny sounding sight'
2. 'hopped home'

questions.question_text: Detail Polynesia's role as a teacher in guiding Dr. Dolittle's transition to veterinary science.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Polynesia acts as an expert instructor. She tests Dr. Dolittle's understanding of basic bird phonetics ('Ka-ka oi-ee, fee-fee'), explains silent animal body language (ear and nose movements), ensures he writes entries in his notebook, and encourages him to apply his knowledge to help animals worldwide.

questions.question_text:
Read the extract from 'A Funny Man' and answer:
'He had two hats upon his feet, / And walked upon his head; / “Good day, Your Highness,” he observed, / And munched a bun of red.'
(a) Describe the man's appearance.
(b) What polite greeting does he use?
(c) What figure of speech is used in 'funny sounding sight'?
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) He wears hats on his feet and walks upside down on his head.
(b) He says, 'Good day, Your Highness'.
(c) Alliteration (repetition of the 's' and 'f' consonant sounds).

questions.question_text: What reason did Dr. Dolittle give for preferring animals over human patients?
options: Option A: Animals pay more money
Option B: Animals do not complain ungratefully
Option C: Animals are easier to catch
questions.correct_answer: Option B: Animals do not complain ungratefully

questions.question_text: Which animal twitches its ears to indicate direction of attention?
What color was the currant bun eaten by the funny man?
Which interjection expresses sudden surprise in Dr. Dolittle's story?
What noun describes Dr. Dolittle after he mastered animal languages?
How did Dr. Dolittle help the old plough horse that could not see well?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Dr. Dolittle examined the horse's eyes, realized it needed spectacles just like humans, and had a special pair of green leather spectacles made for it.

questions.question_text: What makes the funny man's greeting 'Your Highness' humorous?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: It is humorous because the speaker is an ordinary person on the street, making the funny man's formal aristocratic address completely absurd.

questions.question_text: Differentiate between vocal animal speech and silent body language.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Vocal speech consists of spoken sound phonetics ('Ka-ka oi-ee'), while silent body language relies on physical movements like tail wags, ear twitches, and eyelid flutters.

questions.question_text: Analyze how empathy forms the foundation of both prose and poetry selections in Unit 2.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: In 'Animals, Birds, and Dr. Dolittle', empathy allows the doctor to listen to animals as equals, mastering their languages to relieve suffering. In 'A Funny Man', the speaker observes the eccentric stranger with gentle amusement and empathy rather than hostility, celebrating harmless humor and individuality.

questions.question_text: Conduct a comprehensive analysis of animal communication methods described by Polynesia.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Polynesia outlines a two-part communication system: 1. Auditory/Vocal: Bird phonetics with distinct sentence meanings ('Ka-ka oi-ee, fee-fee'). 2. Non-Verbal Signetics: Twitching nostrils for asking questions, moving ears for spatial awareness, and tail movements for emotional states. Understanding both enables true inter-species dialogue.

questions.question_text: Who was the first human patient mentioned in Dr. Dolittle's kitchen?
What ingredient caused the pugs brought by old ladies to get sick?
Which of the following is a hyphenated compound word?
What movement indicates a dog is asking a question quietly?
What literary genre best describes Natalie Joan's 'A Funny Man'?
How did word spread about Dr. Dolittle's ability to speak animal language?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Animals told one another about the doctor who spoke their language, and pet owners and farmers noticed their animals recovering quickly, spreading the news by word of mouth.

questions.question_text: Why is 'butcher's book' an ironic choice of notebook for Dr. Dolittle?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: It is ironic because a butcher's book is normally used for meat sales, but Dr. Dolittle uses it to record animal language to save animal lives.

questions.question_text: Formulate three sentences using present perfect tense verbs.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Dr. Dolittle has recorded new bird words.
2. Polynesia has taught the doctor animal signetics.
3. The funny man has hopped home on his head.

questions.question_text: Roleplay Script Analysis: Write a short doctor-patient dialogue between Dr. Dolittle and a sick pug suffering from eating sweet cake.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Dr. Dolittle: 'Good morning, my little friend. What seems to be troubling your stomach?'
Pug (twitching nose): 'Woof-fee, doctor! My owner feeds me rich chocolate cake every afternoon, and my stomach aches badly.'
Dr. Dolittle: 'I understand completely. I shall prescribe plain porridge and inform your owner that pugs need healthy food, not sugary cake!'

questions.question_text: Exhaustively evaluate the educational values of Unit 2 regarding animal welfare and human communication.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Unit 2 teaches that effective communication requires active, respectful listening. By showing Dr. Dolittle mastering animal languages, the text promotes animal welfare, empathy, and patient-centered care. Furthermore, the grammar lessons on compound words and present perfect tense equip students with practical language tools while enjoying humorous storytelling.

questions.question_text: In Natalie Joan's poem 'A Funny Man', where does the funny man wear his hats?
questions.explanation: The funny man wears two hats on his feet instead of shoes.

questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): Dr. Dolittle decided to learn animal languages from Polynesia.
Reason (R): The Cat's-food-Man pointed out that human patients complain ungratefully and local veterinarians cannot talk to animals.
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
C) (A) is true but (R) is false.
D) (A) is false but (R) is true.
questions.correct_answer: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: The Cat's-food-Man's observation inspired Dr. Dolittle to switch to animal medicine.

questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): Animals communicate exclusively through loud vocal sounds.
Reason (R): Polynesia explains that dogs twitch their nostrils and flap their ears to convey silent messages.
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
C) (A) is false but (R) is true.
D) (A) is true but (R) is false.
questions.correct_answer: C) (A) is false but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Animals do NOT rely exclusively on vocal sounds; body language forms a major part of their communication.

questions.question_text: How did Polynesia demonstrate that birds have a language of their own?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Polynesia translated bird phonetics ('Ka-ka oi-ee, fee-fee') and explained that birds also communicate using non-verbal signs like tail twitches and ear movements. [2 Marks]

questions.question_text: How did Dr. Dolittle record animal vocabulary during his lessons?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: He retrieved his butcher's notebook and pen, writing down bird words and body signetics systematically as Polynesia explained them. [2 Marks]

questions.question_text: Describe two absurd actions performed by the funny man in Natalie Joan's poem.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Wearing hats on his feet instead of shoes. [1 Mark]
2. Hopping home upside down on his head while eating a currant bun. [1 Mark]

questions.question_text: Why did farmers and pet owners prefer bringing their sick animals to Dr. Dolittle?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Because Dr. Dolittle could talk to animals directly, understand their exact complaints, and treat them with tailored empathy rather than guessing. [2 Marks]

sections.section_name: Section C: Character Study & Long Questions

questions.question_text: Analyze Dr. Dolittle as an empathetic healer. How does his willingness to listen transform his professional life?
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Humility & Open Mind: Unlike conventional doctors, he admits human ignorance regarding animal languages. [1 Mark]
2. Dedicated Scholar: Takes systematic notes in his butcher's book to master bird linguistics. [1 Mark]
3. Empathetic Listener: Listens directly to pugs, cows, and plough horses, discovering their true ailments. [1 Mark]
4. Professional Transformation: Moves from an unappreciated human practice to becoming a world-renowned animal doctor. [1 Mark]

questions.question_text: How does Natalie Joan create humor in 'A Funny Man'? Discuss the role of physical inversion and polite dialogue.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Physical Inversion: Reverses normal body postures (hats on feet, walking on head). [1.5 Marks]
2. Linguistic Formality: Contrasts ridiculous physical appearance with courtly address ('Your Highness'). [1.5 Marks]
3. Poetic Rhythm: Uses lively metre and visual imagery to entertain readers. [1 Mark]

questions.case_scenario:
Read the case scenario:
A local animal welfare club wants to train pet owners on how to read animal stress signals. Many owners misinterpret fear gestures (like a dog flattening its ears or hiding) as stubborn disobedience.

sub_questions.sub_q: (a) Based on Polynesia's teachings, what non-verbal signals should pet owners observe?
sub_questions.marking_scheme_answer: Nostril twitching, ear flattening, tail movements, and eyelid flutters. [2 Marks]

sub_questions.sub_q: (b) How can understanding silent animal communication prevent pet mistreatment?
sub_questions.marking_scheme_answer: Owners will recognize fear or pain rather than assuming stubbornness, offering comfort instead of punishment. [2 Marks]

sub_questions.sub_q: (c) Draft a 1-line slogan for the animal welfare campaign inspired by Dr. Dolittle.
sub_questions.marking_scheme_answer: 'Listen with your eyes: Animals speak through love and signs!' (Accept any creative, relevant slogan). [2 Marks]
